Title: Adversarial UV patch attack from implicit 3D face representation via model inversion

## Highlights

*   •
A 3D-aware adversarial patch framework operating directly in UV texture space.

*   •
Identity consistent implicit 3D facial representation recovered via model inversion.

*   •
Multi view differentiable rendering used to optimize UV space perturbations.

*   •
Strong transferability across models and across images of the same victim.

## Abstract

Adversarial patch attacks pose a practical threat to face recognition systems. While most existing methods are formulated in the 2D image space, robust transfer across pose variation and different images of the same victim remains insufficiently addressed. We propose InvUVPatch, a 3D-aware adversarial patch framework that employs a two-stage inversion procedure on a neural-rendering-based 3D generative model to recover identity-consistent implicit facial representations of both the source and target identities. These inversion-derived geometric priors enable direct adversarial optimization in UV texture space. Combined with multi-view differentiable rendering, pose sampling, and similarity transformations, this design enables geometry-aligned optimization for improved target impersonation and cross-image transferability. Experiments on multiple face recognition models show that InvUVPatch achieves strong white-box and black-box performance, improving black-box attack success rates by up to 46.07 percentage points over the strongest baseline. Ablation studies further confirm the contribution of model inversion, UV-space refinement, and geometric augmentation to the effectiveness of the proposed method.

## Introduction

Face recognition (FR) has achieved remarkable progress with the rapid development of deep learning [1], [2], [3]. As a result, FR systems have been widely deployed in security-sensitive applications, such as identity verification, mobile payment, law enforcement, and access control. Despite these advances, extensive studies have shown that deep FR models remain vulnerable to adversarial perturbations [4], [5], [6]. Among these, adversarial patch attacks pose a particularly practical threat because they can be physically realized, do not require access to model internals, and can induce impersonation of a target identity. Therefore, studying more realistic and transferable patch-based impersonation attacks is important for understanding and improving the robustness of modern FR systems.

Most existing adversarial patch attacks are formulated in the 2D image space, where perturbations are directly optimized on source face images [7], [8], [9]. Although effective in digital settings, such methods often lack geometric consistency and tend to degrade under pose or viewpoint changes [10], [11]. In addition, prior studies mainly emphasize cross-model transferability, namely, whether a patch generated for one FR model can transfer to another [12], [13]. By contrast, an equally important but less explored issue is cross-image transferability for the same victim identity. In realistic scenarios, an attacker may only obtain a single portrait of the victim from social media or other online sources, whereas the FR system stores a different image captured under different conditions. This mismatch makes conventional 2D patches fragile and limits their practical effectiveness.

To address this problem, we propose **InvUVPatch**, a 3D-aware adversarial patch framework that combines model inversion with UV-space perturbation learning. Instead of directly refining perturbations in the image plane, InvUVPatch first reconstructs implicit 3D facial representations for both the source and target identities through model inversion. This inversion process provides identity-consistent and geometry-aware latent representations, which serve as the basis for adversarial patch generation. On top of this representation, the adversarial perturbation is optimized in the UV texture space, producing an adversarial UV patch that can be rendered back onto the face under different poses.

To improve transferability and robustness, we further integrate differentiable multi-view rendering into the optimization process. This design enforces both feature-level alignment and multi-view consistency: the rendered adversarial faces are encouraged to approach the target identity in the FR embedding space, while the attack effect is preserved across different viewpoints. Compared with prior patch attacks such as TAP [13] and RSTAM [11], which mainly improve transferability through input-diversity-based optimization in the 2D image space, InvUVPatch integrates identity-consistent model inversion, direct UV-space perturbation learning, and multi-view differentiable rendering into a unified framework, enabling geometry-aligned optimization and improved transferability across pose variations and different images of the same victim.

Our main contributions are summarized as follows:

*   •
We propose InvUVPatch, a 3D-aware adversarial patch framework that integrates identity-consistent model inversion with direct UV-space perturbation learning for face recognition attacks.

*   •
We introduce a geometry-aligned optimization strategy that combines UV-space patch refinement with multi-view differentiable rendering, thereby improving robustness to pose variation and cross-image transferability.

*   •
Extensive experiments show that InvUVPatch consistently outperforms existing adversarial patch baselines in both white-box and black-box settings, while transferring more effectively across different images of the same victim.

## Experiments

In this section, we present the experimental results and analyze the effectiveness of our proposed InvUVPatch method. We benchmark its performance against other adversarial attack methods across a variety of target FR models and systems. A detailed examination of its success in impersonation attacks, emphasizing both effectiveness and transferability, is also included.

## Discussion

InvUVPatch demonstrates that geometry-aligned adversarial optimization in UV space can substantially improve attack transferability for face recognition systems. By combining identity-consistent model inversion, multi-view differentiable rendering, and UV-space perturbation learning, the proposed framework reduces the sensitivity of adversarial patches to pose changes and improves the overall stability of impersonation behavior across different viewpoints and images of the same victim.
